To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
acute, transient inhibition of Bcr-Abl with clinically achievable concentrations of dasatinib or nilotinib results in irreversible commitment to apoptosis in Bcr-Abl dependent CML cells.

acute exposure to clinically achievable concentrations of dasatinib or nilotinib irreversibly commits Bcr-ABl+ CML cells to cell death, and that this effect can be reproduced by transient inhibition of Bcr-Abl using a range of inhibitors.
acute, transient exposure to dasatinib or nilotinib results in irreversible cell death of Bcr-Abl-expressing cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how kinase inhibitors affect cellular signaling networks.
the development of small-molecule kinase inhibitors as novel therapeutic agents for the treatment of cancer.
the mechanisms that underlie the efficacy of Bcr-Abl inhibitors, and how they might be applied to improve the treatment of chronic-phase CML.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the efficacy of dasatinib is due in part to its ability to induce apoptosis in a transient manner.
acute dasatinib exposure is not only sufficient, but also necessary, to induce cell death.
acute dasatinib exposure is sufficient to commit Bcr-Abl-expressing CML cells to apoptosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
transient inhibition of the kinase activity of Bcr-Abl is sufficient to commit CML cells to apoptosis.
acute exposure of cells to dasatinib, or to other Bcr-Abl inhibitors such as nilotinib and imatinib, is sufficient to irreversibly commit Bcr-Abl-positive cells to apoptosis.
acute Bcr-Abl exposure is sufficient to induce cell death.
The main takeaway from our work is that
acute exposure to clinically achievable dasatinub concentrations is sufficient to induce apoptosis and clonal extinction in chronic-phase CML progenitor cells.
acute Bcr-Abl kinase inhibition can be sufficient to achieve maximal therapeutic efficacy.
acute exposure to dasatinib is sufficient to induce apoptosis and clonal cell death.
